title: Redis Operator / RedisCluster
description: Slots, shards, masters and Events of a RedisCluster

list.name: Resharding
list.expr: {namespace="redis-operator-system", container="manager"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster","namespace":"$namespace"\}` != `Moved slot` |~ `reason": "Resharding` | regexp `^\S+\t(?P<level>\S+)\t(?:events\t)?(?P<msg>[^\t]+)` | regexp `"reason": "(?P<reason>[^"]+)"` | regexp `"error": "(?P<error>(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"` | line_format `operator  {{.msg}} {{.reason}} {{.error}}`

target.expr: {namespace="redis-operator-system", container="manager"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster","namespace":"$namespace"\}` != `Moved slot` |~ `reason": "Resharding` | regexp `^\S+\t(?P<level>\S+)\t(?:events\t)?(?P<msg>[^\t]+)` | regexp `"reason": "(?P<reason>[^"]+)"` | regexp `"error": "(?P<error>(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"` | line_format `operator  {{.msg}} {{.reason}} {{.error}}`

list.name: Failover of a shard
list.expr: {namespace="redis-operator-system", container="manager"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` != `Moved slot` |~ `Started (cluster )?failover|reason": "(Switchover|Failover)` | regexp `^\S+\t(?P<level>\S+)\t(?:events\t)?(?P<msg>[^\t]+)` | regexp `"reason": "(?P<reason>[^"]+)"` | regexp `"error": "(?P<error>(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"` | line_format `operator  {{.msg}} {{.reason}} {{.error}}`

target.expr: {namespace="redis-operator-system", container="manager"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` != `Moved slot` |~ `Started (cluster )?failover|reason": "(Switchover|Failover)` | regexp `^\S+\t(?P<level>\S+)\t(?:events\t)?(?P<msg>[^\t]+)` | regexp `"reason": "(?P<reason>[^"]+)"` | regexp `"error": "(?P<error>(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"` | line_format `operator  {{.msg}} {{.reason}} {{.error}}`

list.name: Alerts
list.expr: max by (alertname, severity) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",name=~"$cluster(-[0-9]+)?"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",redis_instance=~"$cluster-[0-9]+"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",persistentvolumeclaim=~"$cluster-[0-9]+-[0-9]+-data"})

list.name: Load test
list.textFormat: A Job with load in its name runs

options.content: **How to read it.** Bars and stats on top are now. The slot map has a row per 256 slots, coloured by the shard that serves them: during a resharding the colours change row by row. Select a range on any graph with the mouse to replay it. Markers: **purple** an Event of the resharding (start, wait, end), **red** a failover or switchover of a shard, **orange** shading while slots move; the switches at the top name them. *Slots moved* counts every slot, however fast it went.

panels.title: Migrating
panels.description: Moving or Waiting (orange), Blocked or Balanced (green: nothing moves)

panels.title: Slots to move
panels.description: status.slotMigration.slotsToMove: 0 once every shard serves its share

panels.title: Shards
panels.description: Shards that exist, also one on its way out

panels.title: Alerts
panels.description: The alerts of config/monitoring/prometheusrule.yaml that fire now or fired in the range; hover a bar for the labels. Nothing here: none fired.

targets.expr: max by (alertname) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",name=~"$cluster(-[0-9]+)?"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",redis_instance=~"$cluster-[0-9]+"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",persistentvolumeclaim=~"$cluster-[0-9]+-[0-9]+-data"}) or (max by (alertname) (max_over_time((ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",name=~"$cluster(-[0-9]+)?"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",redis_instance=~"$cluster-[0-9]+"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",persistentvolumeclaim=~"$cluster-[0-9]+-[0-9]+-data"})[$__range:15s])) * 0 - 1)

panels.title: Slots per shard now
panels.description: 16384 slots split between the shards; equal when balanced

panels.title: Slots per shard over time
panels.description: The lines meet at 16384 / shards when the resharding is done

panels.title: Slots moved, from shard to shard
panels.description: Every slot the operator moved, counted, so none is missed between two scrapes

panels.title: Slots moved in the time range
Conditions: one row each, the text is the reason
panels.description: Ready, SlotsCovered and Migrating, one row each; the bar shows the reason over time. Green: fine. Grey: idle (Balanced). Orange: slots move or wait (Moving, Waiting, Resharding). Red: a problem (Blocked, SlotsUncovered, ...).

panels.title: Which shard serves the slots (a row per 256 slots)
panels.description: Every row is a block of 256 slots, coloured by the shard that serves most of them

panels.title: Operations: everything the operator (and the Instance Managers) did to it
Switchovers
panels.description: Completed planned moves of the primary of the masters of the shards (by the operator; Redis Cluster fails over on its own too)

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind | drop fields |= `"kind": "switchover"` !~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Failovers
panels.description: Failovers of the masters of the shards (by the operator; Redis Cluster fails over on its own too)

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind | drop fields |= `"kind": "failover"` [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Rejected or failed
panels.description: Switchovers and recreates the operator rejected (e.g. a target that is not Ready, the primary), that failed (the target did not catch up in a minute) or that a failover interrupted

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind | drop fields |~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Slowest switchover
panels.description: From the start of the switchover until the target is the primary

targets.expr: max(max_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, durationMs | drop fields |= `"kind": "switchover"` !~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` | unwrap durationMs [$__range]))

panels.title: Slowest failover
panels.description: From the start of the failover until the target is the primary

targets.expr: max(max_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, durationMs | drop fields |= `"kind": "failover"` !~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` | unwrap durationMs [$__range]))

panels.title: Longest primary outage
panels.description: How long a primary was unavailable before a failover or a safe start ended

targets.expr: max(max_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, downMs | drop fields | unwrap downMs [$__range]))

panels.title: Every operation (click one for its logs)
panels.description: One row per switchover, failover, rolling update, safe start, recreate (asked for), volume replaced (a PVC of a replica deleted or lost), configuration (spec.redis applied or rejected by Redis), certificate (issued or updated), scale up or down, and self-fence (the Instance Manager paused the writes of the primary while it could not reach the API server), from the line logged when it ends, with its outcome and why it started. Took: from its start to its end; for a volume, until the replica is Ready again on the new one, after its full sync. Primary down: for a failover or a safe start, since the primary became unavailable. Click the kind of a row: the dashboard opens on the seconds of that operation, and *What happened, to the millisecond* shows every log line of it, of the operator and of the Pods.

targets.expr: {namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, outcome, name, from, to, epoch, durationMs, downMs, reason, startMs, endMs | label_format linkFrom=`{{ if .startMs }}{{ sub .startMs 3000 }}{{ end }}`, linkTo=`{{ if .endMs }}{{ add .endMs 5000 }}{{ end }}`, outcome=`{{ or .outcome "completed" }}`, inst=`{{ .name }}` | drop fields

panels.title: How long each one took
panels.description: A point per operation at the moment it ended; the height is how long it took (log scale)

targets.expr: max by (kind) (max_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster-[0-9]+","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, durationMs | drop fields !~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` | unwrap durationMs [$__interval]))

panels.title: Replication: masters, replicas and where they run
panels.description: Every node with its machine and commands per second (green a master, blue a replica); every arrow a replica, with the bytes per second it replicates.

targets.expr: sum by (id, title, subtitle, color) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(sum by (pod, node, role) ((rate(redis_commands_processed_total{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}[$__rate_interval]) and redis_commands_processed_total{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}) * on (pod) group_left (node) max by (pod, pod_ip, node) (kube_pod_info{namespace="$namespace",pod=~"$cluster-[0-9]+-[0-9]+"})), "id", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "title", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "subtitle", "$1", "node", "(.*)"), "color", "green", "role", "primary"), "color", "blue", "role", "replica"))

sum by (id, source, target) (label_join(label_replace(label_replace(sum by (pod, slave_ip) (deriv(redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}[$__rate_interval]) and redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}) * on (slave_ip) group_left (replica) label_replace(label_replace(max by (pod, pod_ip, node) (kube_pod_info{namespace="$namespace",pod=~"$cluster-[0-9]+-[0-9]+"}), "replica", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "slave_ip", "$1", "pod_ip", "(.*)"), "source", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "target", "$1", "replica", "(.*)"), "id", "->", "source", "target"))

panels.title: Replication throughput per replica
panels.description: Bytes per second each replica takes from its primary: the write traffic of the primary

targets.expr: sum by (pod, slave_ip) ((deriv(redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (pod, slave_ip) redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}) * on (slave_ip) group_left (replica) label_replace(label_replace(max by (pod, pod_ip, node) (kube_pod_info{namespace="$namespace",pod=~"$cluster-[0-9]+-[0-9]+"}), "replica", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "slave_ip", "$1", "pod_ip", "(.*)")

panels.title: Lag of every replica
panels.description: The most bytes of writes the replica had not acknowledged in each minute, as its primary sees it. A replica acknowledges once a second, so up to a second of writes is normal; a line that keeps growing is a replica that falls behind.

targets.expr: sum by (pod, slave_ip) ((max_over_time((max by (pod) (redis_master_repl_offset{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}) - on (pod) group_right redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"})[1m:])) and on (pod, slave_ip) redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}) * on (slave_ip) group_left (replica) label_replace(label_replace(max by (pod, pod_ip, node) (kube_pod_info{namespace="$namespace",pod=~"$cluster-[0-9]+-[0-9]+"}), "replica", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "slave_ip", "$1", "pod_ip", "(.*)")

panels.title: Resyncs served in the time range
panels.description: Full: the primary sent a whole snapshot (a new or a lost replica). Partial: a replica caught up from the backlog, e.g. after a switchover.

panels.title: Masters per machine
panels.description: More than one master on a machine: losing it takes them all at once, and with them a majority of the cluster (alert RedisClusterMastersOnOneMachine). podAntiAffinityType keeps the Pods of one shard apart, not the masters of different shards.

targets.expr: count by (node) (max by (pod) (redis_operator_cluster_shard_primary{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"} == 1) * on (pod) group_left (node) max by (pod, node) (kube_pod_info{namespace="$namespace"}))

panels.title: Main thread busy
panels.description: Redis runs commands on one thread: at 100 % a node can do no more, however many cores the machine has. Add shards, not CPUs.

panels.title: CPU throttled by the limit
panels.description: Share of the time the kernel held Redis back for its CPU limit: latency spikes even when the average looks fine. Empty without a CPU limit.

panels.title: Commands per second, every master
panels.description: Lines far apart: a hot shard, with hot keys or more slots; Redis 7.2 has no numbers per slot

panels.title: Busiest master / average
panels.description: 1: the load is even; 2: one shard does twice the average and reaches its ceiling first

targets.expr: max(sum by (redis_instance) (rate(redis_commands_processed_total{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (namespace, pod) (redis_operator_instance_pod_role{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance=~"$cluster-[0-9]+"} == 1))) / avg(sum by (redis_instance) (rate(redis_commands_processed_total{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}[$__rate_interval]) and on (namespace, pod) (redis_operator_instance_pod_role{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance=~"$cluster-[0-9]+"} == 1)))

panels.title: Memory of every master, of maxmemory
panels.description: At 100 %: with noeviction writes fail with OOM (see the errors), with an allkeys-* policy keys are evicted

targets.expr: max by (namespace, pod) (redis_memory_used_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}) / max by (namespace, pod) (redis_memory_max_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}) and on (namespace, pod) (redis_operator_instance_pod_role{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance=~"$cluster-[0-9]+"} == 1)

panels.title: Container memory, of its limit
panels.description: maxmemory plus the copy of a fork (BGSAVE, AOF rewrite, full resync), client and replica buffers: at 100 % the kernel OOMKills Redis

panels.title: Network of every node
panels.description: Clients, replication and MIGRATE; the cluster bus has its own port

panels.title: Output buffers
panels.description: A replica over the soft limit for a minute, or over the hard one, is dropped and comes back with a full resync, which under load may repeat. The hard limit (256 MB by default) may be above the memory limit of the Pod.

panels.title: Seconds of writes the backlog holds
panels.description: A replica cut off for longer than this needs a full resync instead of a partial one. Seconds under heavy writes: raise repl-backlog-size in spec.redis.parameters.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, pod) (redis_config_repl_backlog_size{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}) / (max by (namespace, pod) (deriv(redis_master_repl_offset{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}[1m])) > 0) and on (namespace, pod) (redis_operator_instance_pod_role{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance=~"$cluster-[0-9]+"} == 1)

panels.title: Changes of the master
panels.description: A bar without a red marker (Failover of a shard) is a failover Redis Cluster made on its own: a master that did not answer for cluster-node-timeout, e.g. busy or forking under load.

panels.title: Stalls, against cluster-node-timeout
panels.description: How long Redis stopped: the last fork, and the latest spike of every kind from LATENCY LATEST (set latency-monitor-threshold, e.g. 100 ms, in spec.redis.parameters). A stall near cluster-node-timeout lets the other masters fail the node over.

panels.title: Restarts in the time range
panels.description: Of the redis container; kubectl describe pod tells OOMKilled

panels.title: Errors Redis answered, by error
panels.description: What clients got back: READONLY right after a switchover, NOREPLICAS with minReplicasToWrite, WRONGPASS or NOPERM for users, MOVED and ASK while slots move, CLUSTERDOWN, BUSYKEY. Commands of the operator count too (e.g. an ERR of a refused parameter).

panels.title: Link of every replica to its master
panels.description: Red: the replica has lost its master (master_link_status:down), e.g. after the master restarted on a new IP. A replica can be Ready while its link is down.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Reads that found their key; empty while nothing reads

panels.title: Evicted and expired keys per second
panels.description: Evicted: removed to stay below maxmemory (maxmemoryPolicy); with noeviction writes fail instead. Expired: their TTL ran out

panels.title: Latency p99, by command
panels.description: Time Redis spent on a command, without the network; the commands of the operator and the exporter are left out

panels.title: Slow log entries
panels.description: Commands slower than slowlog-log-slower-than (10 ms); read them with SLOWLOG GET

panels.title: Memory fragmentation
panels.description: RSS / used memory: about 1 to 1.5 is fine; above, memory is lost to fragmentation; below 1, swapping

panels.title: Last fork took
panels.description: Redis stops while it forks for an RDB save, an AOF rewrite or a full resync; grows with the dataset

panels.title: Saving in the background
panels.description: 1 while an RDB save or an AOF rewrite runs

panels.title: Rejected connections and blocked clients
panels.description: Rejected: over maxclients. Blocked: clients waiting in BLPOP, XREAD BLOCK, WAIT

panels.title: cluster_state, seen by every node
panels.description: Every node judges the cluster on its own: one red row is a node cut off from the others

panels.title: Slots in trouble and nodes known, seen by every node
panels.description: pfail: a node thinks the master of the slots is down; fail: the masters agree. Known nodes above the nodes that run: an ID not forgotten yet

panels.title: Keys by type and memory, now
panels.description: Every Pod samples 200 random keys at every scrape (RANDOMKEY, TYPE, MEMORY USAGE) and counts them by type and memory: a share of the keys, not exact. A rare type or a few big keys may not show; redis-cli --bigkeys finds those.

targets.expr: sum by (key) (avg by (redis_instance, key) (redis_script_values{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"})) / scalar(sum(avg by (redis_instance, key) (redis_script_values{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"})))

panels.title: Keys by type over time
panels.description: Share of the sampled keys by type; with Keys it tells how many of each

targets.expr: sum by (type) (label_replace(avg by (redis_instance, key) (redis_script_values{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"}), "type", "$1", "key", "(\\S+) .*")) / scalar(sum(avg by (redis_instance, key) (redis_script_values{namespace="$namespace",redis_cluster="$cluster"})))

panels.title: Volumes used
panels.description: Used space of every PVC, from the kubelet; orange from 70 %, red from 85 %

panels.title: AOF size
panels.description: The append-only file grows with every write and shrinks at a rewrite

panels.title: Since the last RDB save
panels.description: How old the snapshot on the volume is; with persistence aof the AOF has the writes since

panels.title: What happened, to the millisecond
panels.description: The log of the operator about the cluster and its shards, without the line of every moved slot: resharding, failovers, nodes that join or are forgotten.

targets.expr: {namespace="redis-operator-system", container="manager"} |~ `\{"name":"$cluster(-[0-9]+)?","namespace":"$namespace"\}` != `Moved slot` | regexp `^\S+\t(?P<level>\S+)\t(?:events\t)?(?P<msg>[^\t]+)` | regexp `"reason": "(?P<reason>[^"]+)"` | regexp `"error": "(?P<error>(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"` | line_format `operator  {{.msg}} {{.reason}} {{.error}}`

panels.title: Role of every node
panels.description: Green: the master of its shard. A green bar jumping rows is a failover.

panels.title: Keys per shard (masters)
panels.description: Keys follow their slots during a resharding
